description: Players can mine only Dirt and Wood. Add Stone as a third resource that the player mines by clicking. One click gives 1 Stone. Append Stone, with the id `stone`, to the end of the `resources` array in `src/resources.ts`.
acceptance: The page lists Stone below Dirt and Wood, with a Mine button.
From a new game, one click on the Mine button for Stone shows 1 Stone and leaves every other amount at 0.
A save written before this change still loads and shows 0 Stone.
`test/game.test.ts` has a test that calls `mine(initialState, "stone")` and asserts the exact resulting state.
`npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, and `npm run build` pass.

summary: Add a Wooden axe that makes Wood every second
description: Nothing makes Wood on its own yet. Add a Wooden axe upgrade. It costs 15 Wood and makes 1 Wood per second for each axe the player owns. Append it, with the id `woodenAxe`, to the end of the `upgrades` array in `src/upgrades.ts`.
acceptance: The page lists a Wooden axe below the Wooden pickaxe, showing `Cost: 15 Wood` and `Makes: 1 Wood per second`.
With 15 Wood, buying a Wooden axe leaves 0 Wood and 1 Wooden axe owned.
With 14 Wood, the Buy button for the Wooden axe is disabled.
With 2 Wooden axes owned, one tick adds 2 Wood.
`test/game.test.ts` has a test for buying a Wooden axe and a test for a tick with 2 of them, each asserting the exact resulting state.
`npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, and `npm run build` pass.

summary: Add a Furnace that burns Wood into Charcoal
description: Add Charcoal, a resource that the player cannot mine by hand, and a Furnace upgrade that makes it. A Furnace costs 20 Dirt and 10 Wood. On each tick, every upgrade that uses no resource produces first. Then each Furnace burns 2 Wood into 1 Charcoal, but only when 2 Wood are left for it. The Furnace is the first upgrade that uses up a resource, so `tick` in `src/game.ts` needs a new rule, and `upgradeDetails` in `src/format.ts` needs a `Uses:` line. Append Charcoal, with the id `charcoal`, to the end of `resources`, and the Furnace, with the id `furnace`, to the end of `upgrades`.
acceptance: The page lists Charcoal below Dirt and Wood, with no Mine button.
The page lists a Furnace below the Wooden pickaxe, showing `Cost: 20 Dirt, 10 Wood`, `Uses: 2 Wood per second`, and `Makes: 1 Charcoal per second`.
With 1 Furnace and 5 Wood, one tick leaves 3 Wood and 1 Charcoal.
With 2 Furnaces and 3 Wood, one tick leaves 1 Wood and 1 Charcoal.
With 1 Furnace and 1 Wood, one tick changes nothing.
`test/game.test.ts` covers each of the three ticks above, and `test/format.test.ts` covers the Furnace's lines, each asserting the exact result.
`npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, and `npm run build` pass.

summary: Show large amounts in short form, like 1.2K
description: Amounts are hard to read once they reach the thousands. Show resource amounts and upgrade costs in short form, with one decimal place and a K, M, or B suffix, and drop a trailing `.0`. Round down, so the page never shows more than the player has. Write the formatter as a pure function in `src/format.ts`, test it in `test/format.test.ts`, and use it for every resource amount and upgrade cost on the page.
acceptance: `0` shows as `0`, and `999` shows as `999`.
`1000` shows as `1K`, `1234` shows as `1.2K`, and `999999` shows as `999.9K`.
With 1234 Dirt saved, the Dirt row on the page shows `1.2K`.
An upgrade that costs 1500 Wood shows `Cost: 1.5K Wood`.
`test/format.test.ts` asserts the exact string for every value above.
`npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, and `npm run build` pass.

summary: Add a Reset button that starts a new game
description: Players have no way to start over. Add a Reset button below the upgrade list. The button asks for confirmation first. After the player confirms, the game returns to `initialState` and overwrites the save, so a reload also shows the new game.
acceptance: The page shows a Reset button below the upgrade list.
Clicking Reset opens a confirmation dialog that reads `Start a new game? Your progress will be lost.`
Confirming sets every resource amount and every owned count on the page to 0.
With no upgrades owned, cancelling leaves every resource amount and every owned count unchanged.
After a confirmed reset, reloading the page still shows 0 for every resource amount and every owned count.
`npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, and `npm run build` pass.

summary: Earn resources while the page is closed
description: Upgrades stop working when the player closes the tab. When the game loads a save, apply one tick for each whole second since the game wrote the save, up to 8 hours. Write the save time into the saved text beside the state, and keep `GameState` unchanged. Add the catch-up rule to `src/game.ts` as a pure function that takes a state and the elapsed milliseconds and calls `tick` once for each missed second, so every upgrade rule applies. Read the clock only in `src/main.ts`.
acceptance: A save written 10 seconds ago with 1 Wooden pickaxe and 0 Dirt loads with 10 Dirt.
A save written 9.5 seconds ago with 1 Wooden pickaxe and 0 Dirt loads with 9 Dirt.
A save written 2 days ago with 1 Wooden pickaxe and 0 Dirt loads with 28800 Dirt, which is 8 hours of ticks.
A save written before this change has no save time, and it loads with no ticks applied.
A save whose time is in the future loads with no ticks applied.
Tests cover each case above and assert the exact resulting state.
`npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, and `npm run build` pass.
